title: Implement RFC 6901 JSON Pointer get/set/remove
prompt:
src/pointer.mjs is a stub. Implement RFC 6901 JSON Pointer support with these exports:

- parse(pointer) -> array of reference tokens. "" is the whole document (no tokens). Any other pointer must start with '/'. Unescape ~1 to '/' and ~0 to '~' (so "~01" means the literal "~1"). A '~' not followed by 0 or 1 is an error.
- compile(tokens) -> pointer string (inverse of parse).
- get(doc, pointer) -> the referenced value, or undefined if the path does not exist (missing key, index out of range, or '-'). Only own properties count: get({}, '/constructor') is undefined.
- set(doc, pointer, value) -> mutates doc and returns it; set(doc, '', v) returns v. On arrays, an index equal to the length or '-' appends; a larger index is an error. A missing parent container is an error (no auto-creation).
- remove(doc, pointer) -> deletes the target and returns the removed value; array elements are spliced out. Removing a path that does not exist is an error, as is removing the root.

Array indices must be '0' or a decimal number without leading zeros; anything else ('01', '1e0', '-1', ' 1') used against an array is an error for set/remove and yields undefined for get. Malformed pointers throw in every function. Errors are thrown as Error instances. Run `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`.
